# The problem

## Using the `Test` standard library

```{.julia code-line-numbers="|3,10|4-9"}
using MyPackage, Test

@testset "MyPackage" begin
    include("core.jl")
    include("linalg.jl")
    include("io.jl")
    include("serialization.jl")
    include("integration.jl")
    # ...
end
```

* One process
* One file after the other, top to bottom

## Limitations

* Wall-clock time grows linearly with the size of the test suite
* CI machines have many cores... mostly idle
* State leaks between `include`d files (`using`, globals, method redefinitions)
* A failure at minute 40 wastes the previous 39 minutes
* Running *only* `linalg.jl` means editing `runtests.jl`

Various packages in the ecosystem already tried to address some of these shortcomings (more on this later)

# `ParallelTestRunner.jl`

## Lineage

* Julia's [`Base.runtests`](https://docs.julialang.org/en/v1/stdlib/Test/#Base.runtests) parallel harness
* adapted by Tim Besard ([`@maleadt`](https://github.com/maleadt)) for CUDA.jl's test infrastructure...
* ...and copied in all other packages of the GPU ecosystem
* extracted and generalised as [JuliaTesting/ParallelTestRunner.jl](https://github.com/JuliaTesting/ParallelTestRunner.jl) by Valentin Churavy ([`@vchuravy`](https://github.com/vchuravy)) + many other contributors
* Purpose-built for large, slow, resource-hungry suites
* Used by CUDA.jl, AMDGPU.jl, Enzyme.jl, and more

## Migration is a deletion

:::: {.columns}

::: {.column width="50%"}
Before:

```{.julia code-line-numbers="false"}
using MyPackage, Test

@testset "MyPackage" begin
    include("core.jl")
    include("linalg.jl")
    include("io.jl")
    # ...
end
```
:::

::: {.column width="50%"}
After:

```{.julia code-line-numbers="false"}
using MyPackage
using ParallelTestRunner

runtests(MyPackage, ARGS)
```
:::

::::

* Every `.jl` file in `test/` (except `runtests.jl`) is autodiscovered as an independent test
* No macros, no annotations, no rewrite of the test files themselves

## Execution model

* Each test file runs in a separate worker *process* ([`JuliaPluto/Malt.jl`](https://github.com/JuliaPluto/Malt.jl))
* ...inside a freshly generated sandbox module: isolation for free
* Results are streamed back to the main process as they complete
* `--jobs=N` controls the number of parallel workers

**File-level parallelism**: coarser than `ReTestItems.jl`'s per-`@testitem` scheduling, but requires no code changes

## A command-line interface

```{.default code-line-numbers="false"}
Usage: runtests.jl [--help] [--list] [--jobs=N] [TESTS...]

   --help             Show this text.
   --list             List all available tests.
   --verbose          Print more information during testing.
   --quickfail        Fail the entire run as soon as a single test errored.
   --jobs=N           Launch `N` processes to perform tests.

   Remaining arguments filter the tests that will be executed.
```

* `julia --project test/runtests.jl linalg` runs only tests whose name starts with `linalg`
* Also works through `Pkg.test(test_args=["linalg"])`

## What it looks like

<!-- The live status bar is only rendered on a TTY, so this is captured from a
real terminal rather than executed at render time. -->

```{.default code-line-numbers="false"}
Running 3 tests using 2 parallel jobs.
                 │   Test   │ ──────────────── CPU ──────────────── │
Test    (Worker) │ time (s) │ GC (s) │ GC % │ Alloc (MB) │ RSS (MB) │
strings      (1) │     0.14 │   0.00 │  0.0 │       6.90 │   454.56 │
arithmetic   (2) │     0.15 │   0.00 │  0.0 │       7.64 │   454.56 │

Running:  slow
Progress: 2/3 tests completed │ ETA: ~0 min
```

* Live status bar: running tests, per-worker stats, ETA
* Worker output is captured and printed without interleaving

## Scheduling smarts

* Duration and pass/fail history of each test is persisted in a scratch directory
* Longest-running tests are scheduled first for better load balancing
* Previously-failing tests are scheduled first to fail fast on re-runs
* Workers exceeding a memory threshold (`max_worker_rss`) are recycled
* ~Zero configuration required

## Escape hatches{.smaller}

* `testsuite`: provide your own `name => code` dictionary instead of autodiscovery (for example if some test files should be always excluded, or be run conditionally)
* `init_code` / `init_worker_code`: set up each sandbox module / each worker
* `test_worker`: create a custom worker (for example with specific environment variables, or different Julia flags)
* `RecordType` + `custom_args`: collect domain-specific metrics per test (how the GPU packages track device memory)
* `exename` / `exeflags` / `env`: control how workers are launched

# Demo

## A toy package

:::: {.columns}

::: {.column width="45%"}
```{.default code-line-numbers="false"}
demo
├── Project.toml
├── src
│   └── Demo.jl
└── test
    ├── arithmetic.jl
    ├── Project.toml
    ├── runtests.jl
    ├── slow.jl
    └── strings.jl
```
:::

::: {.column width="55%"}
`test/runtests.jl`:

```{.julia code-line-numbers="false"}
using Demo, ParallelTestRunner

runtests(Demo, ARGS)
```
:::

::::

`test/arithmetic.jl`, `test/strings.jl`, `test/slow.jl` are plain `Test` files, no `include` anywhere

```{julia}
function run_demo(args...)
    project = Base.active_project()
    dir = joinpath(dirname(project), "demo", "test")
    cmd = `$(Base.julia_cmd()) --project=$(project) runtests.jl $(collect(args))`
    print(readchomp(ignorestatus(setenv(cmd; dir))))
end
nothing
```

## Parallel run{.scrollable}

`julia --project test/runtests.jl --jobs=2 --verbose`

```{julia}
run_demo("--jobs=2", "--verbose")
```

# Choosing testing package

## Comparison{.smaller}

|                         | Parallelism        | Rewrite        | Isolation  | Filtering  |
|-------------------------|--------------------|----------------|------------|------------|
| `Test`                  | ❌                 | —              | ❌         | ❌         |
| `SafeTestsets.jl`       | ❌                 | `@safetestset` | ✅         | ❌         |
| `TestItemRunner.jl`     | ❌                 | `@testitem`    | ✅         | tags       |
| `ReTestItems.jl`        | ✅ procs, per item | `@testitem`    | ✅         | name, tags |
| `XUnit.jl`              | ✅ threads         | `@testcase`    | ❌         | ✅         |
| `ParallelTestRunner.jl` | ✅ procs, per file | ~none          | ✅         | prefix     |

## When to choose what

* Existing `include`-style suite, want parallelism with zero rewrite → `ParallelTestRunner.jl`
* Sub-file granularity, retries for flaky tests, tags → `ReTestItems.jl`
* Heavy VS Code test-explorer user → `TestItems.jl` + `TestItemRunner.jl`
* Need JUnit XML reports, or thread-based parallelism → `XUnit.jl`
* Small, fast suite → plain `Test` is fine!

## What `ParallelTestRunner.jl` doesn't do (yet)

* No automatic retries of flaky tests (pending PR [#148](https://github.com/JuliaTesting/ParallelTestRunner.jl/pull/148))
* Only prefix-based *inclusion* filters, no exclusion (issue [#134](https://github.com/JuliaTesting/ParallelTestRunner.jl/issues/134))
* No JUnit XML output
* No editor integration

Contributions welcome!

# Conclusions

* Parallelism + isolation + a CLI, for the price of *deleting* code
* Battle-tested: [used](https://github.com/search?q=%2Fusing.*+ParallelTestRunner%2F+language%3AJulia++NOT+is%3Aarchived+NOT+is%3Afork+path%3A%2F%5Etest%5C%2Fruntests.jl%2F&type=code) by over 80 packages already
* Give it a try:
    * [github.com/JuliaTesting/ParallelTestRunner.jl](https://github.com/JuliaTesting/ParallelTestRunner.jl)
    * [juliatesting.github.io/ParallelTestRunner.jl](https://juliatesting.github.io/ParallelTestRunner.jl/)
